questions.stem: A plant wants a metric that can trigger corrective action before an injury occurs. Which proposed measure best meets that purpose?
options: Total recordable injury rate
Percentage of high-risk corrective actions verified effective by the due date
Number of lost-time cases last year
Workers compensation cost already incurred
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A leading indicator measures preventive activity or control performance that can be acted on before harm occurs.
incorrectOptionExplanations: TRIR summarizes outcomes that have already occurred.
Lost-time cases are lagging outcomes.
Paid or incurred loss cost is a retrospective consequence.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, leading versus lagging indicators, pp. 810-816; OSHA leading indicators

questions.stem: One plant reports 20 hazards corrected and another reports 35, but their workforce and reporting volume differ greatly. What is needed for a fair comparison?
options: Rank plants only by the raw count
Remove the smaller plant from the comparison
Normalize the measure to an appropriate exposure or opportunity denominator and retain context
Convert every measure to dollars
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Rates or proportions tied to hours, tasks, reports, or relevant opportunities improve comparability while context prevents misuse.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Raw counts can reflect size and reporting opportunity rather than performance.
Excluding a site avoids analysis instead of improving it.
Financial conversion is not appropriate for every safety activity.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, measurement methods and quantitative indicators, pp. 797-816

questions.stem: A bonus depends only on zero recordable injuries, and near-miss reports suddenly fall to zero. What should management suspect?
options: All hazards have been eliminated
Near-miss reporting is no longer useful
The bonus proves safety culture improved
The measure may be suppressing reporting and creating a misleading signal
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Measures shape behavior; poorly designed incentives can reward concealment rather than learning and prevention.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Zero reports do not establish zero hazards.
Near-miss information remains valuable when reporting is trusted and analyzed.
An incentive can change reporting behavior without changing risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, problems with injury statistics, leading indicators, and culture measures, pp. 797-816

questions.stem: Which performance target is most actionable?
options: Cut critical-hazard closure time from 20 to 10 days by Q4 and verify effectiveness
Improve safety performance as soon as resources and operational conditions permit
Reduce the number of safety problems reported across all departments during the year
Complete the largest possible number of corrective actions without classifying their risk
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A useful target is specific, measurable, time-bound, relevant to risk, and paired with quality or effectiveness evidence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This lacks a baseline, target, timeframe, and verification method.
The statement is vague and not measurable.
Volume alone can reward low-value closure and ignore effectiveness.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, why, what, when, and how to measure performance, pp. 799-816

questions.stem: Which dashboard gives the strongest picture of safety-system performance?
options: Injury-frequency rates alone, compared with the prior year and industry averages
Hazard trends, control health, participation, action effectiveness, and outcome rates
Training-attendance totals alone, grouped by department and employee classification
Audit-finding totals alone, without considering severity, recurrence, or corrective action
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Balanced measures connect risk, implementation, control effectiveness, learning, and outcomes.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One lagging outcome cannot show whether current risk and controls are improving.
Attendance does not prove competence, transfer, or risk reduction.
Finding count depends on scope and reporting and does not alone show system health.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, performance measurement and leading indicators, pp. 797-816

questions.stem: Which measure best monitors the health of local exhaust ventilation?
options: Number of fans painted this year
Total electricity used by all buildings
Percentage of systems meeting verified capture and airflow criteria on schedule
Number of ventilation procedures printed
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A control-health indicator should directly test whether the critical engineering control performs within defined limits.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Paint does not demonstrate airflow or capture performance.
Energy use is indirect and affected by many unrelated loads.
Document count does not show physical control effectiveness.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 9 and 36, ventilation performance and leading indicators, pp. 294-313 and 797-816

questions.stem: TRIR falls while serious near misses and overdue critical actions rise. What is the best interpretation?
options: Overall risk definitely decreased
Near misses should be ignored because no injury occurred
Overdue actions improve the reliability of TRIR
The lagging rate alone may mask increasing risk and weakening preventive performance
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Multiple indicators should be interpreted together, especially when leading and potential-severity evidence conflicts with lagging results.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One outcome rate cannot override adverse risk and control signals.
Near misses can reveal high-consequence pathways before loss.
Overdue actions indicate unresolved risk, not improved rate reliability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, leading and lagging indicators and near misses, pp. 810-816

questions.stem: A culture survey has only 12% participation, mostly from managers. What limitation should be reported?
options: The result may not represent the workforce and is vulnerable to nonresponse bias
Low participation automatically proves poor culture
Manager responses should be multiplied to represent workers
The survey is exact because it is anonymous
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Survey interpretation should disclose participation, respondent mix, method, uncertainty, and follow-up evidence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Low response is a limitation but does not by itself prove the underlying culture score.
Weighting cannot replace missing perspectives without a defensible sampling design.
Anonymity can improve candor but does not eliminate representativeness problems.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, employee perceptions and measurement methods, pp. 797-816

questions.stem: A site reports 98% corrective-action closure, but many actions are reopened. Which additional measure is most useful?
options: Total number of emails about actions
Percentage of closed actions verified effective and sustained after an appropriate interval
Average length of action descriptions
Number of users with dashboard access
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Effectiveness and recurrence measures distinguish administrative closure from genuine risk reduction.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Communication volume does not prove corrective effectiveness.
Description length is not a quality outcome.
System access does not show the action controlled the risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 36, safety-related work orders and continuous improvement, pp. 810-816

questions.stem: What should accompany every key safety performance measure?
options: A different formula at each site
No owner so the metric remains independent
A defined purpose, calculation, data source, owner, frequency, target, and required response
A target that can be changed after results are known
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A controlled metric definition ensures consistency, accountability, interpretation, and action.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Inconsistent definitions prevent valid comparison and trend analysis.
Without ownership, adverse trends may not trigger action.
Changing targets after seeing results undermines integrity.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
